steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Signora Venezia, did you just say my child was taken away by Venezia wise guys?

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: My informant has no reason to lie to me.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: It's true Luchino went to the port area that night. I heard a car accident happened.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: Yes, I was nearby as well.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: I'm guessing the Venezias are involved, and if I'm not wrong, Luchino should have discovered something.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: *sigh*

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Please leave, Signora. I have to close the shop early today.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: You're going to find Venezia Junior yourself?

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: Umberto, I don't know what you used to be like. But I'm sure your age has affected your abilities, even if you were chosen by Vargo back then.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: A sickly old tailor might not even make it past Venezia Junior's doorstep.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: If Luchino really found out about something he shouldn't have, then he might be stuck at the Venezia estate for good.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: I'm old and feeble, Signora Venezia. Even if this hadn't happened, my candle's burning out anyway.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: If there's anything I can't let go right now, it's the boy.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: He's my only relative, and I am his only relative too. He's still so young. Children always leave us with no other choice.

spans.text: He's my only relative, and I am
only relative too. He's still so young. Children always leave us with no other choice.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Besides, I'm no stranger to the Venezias.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: I didn't tell you this before—but I used to work for them before you did.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: It's probably why Vargo chose me.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: *sigh* Life goes in a circle, and now I'm going back to where I used to be.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: I'll go with you.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Signora... this has nothing to do with you at all.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: I'm already very grateful you found a clue to his whereabouts, and came here just to let me know.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: I know you had an unpleasant split with the Venezias because of what happened with Lisa, so if you go back just like that, you'll run into all sorts of trouble.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: You need not worry. I'm doing this because of my agreement with Vargo. Before I find out what truly happened back then, I won't allow anything to happen to you.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: Besides, I understand what sacrifices one would willingly make for the sake of a child.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: Is someone there? Can I leave now?
A child?

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: Did you say something, ragazzino?

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: Afraid of me?

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: May I go home, per favore?

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: I'm afraid I just happen to be here as a guest, so I can't interfere in family matters. Why are they keeping you in here?

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: I-I don't know, but if you can't let me go... could you at least contact Umberto de Montano of De Montano Tailor Shop for me?

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: Umberto...

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: He's my nonno. He'll get worried if I'm gone for too long... I have some medicine for him I got from the shop which he really needs, if I c-can't...

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: You're worried about your nonno?

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: Mhm.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: Follow me. The Venezias always treat their guests right.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: I didn't think I'd meet a friend on this trip.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: Lucky for me, I like it when it's lively.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: Do I just follow you...? But those people outside...

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: They're also busy catering to me, their guest.
Luchino follows the old man close behind, and they don't run into anyone on their way.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: Wh-Who exactly are you, if you don't mind me asking?

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: Stay close, boy. It's a big place, but we're almost there.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: Earlier you said you wanted me to tell your nonno about a bunch of things, right?

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: Sorry, I'm old and my memory's spotty.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: But I think you can tell him yourself.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: Umberto, I envy you for having such a loving grandson.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: N-Nonno?
Luchino's head is full of questions—Has he interrupted De Montano's business? Was his nonno worried sick about him? How did he know to find him here?
Umberto only casts a glance at Luchino. The old tailor doesn't say a word.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: Have a seat.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: I'll decline. My legs aren't as good as they used to. Sitting down is easy, but getting up is quite difficult.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: Alright then.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: You said Ingrid came with you... so where is she?

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: She left after learning you were the one who found Luchino. She really trusts you.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: ...Alright.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: When did you move out of Montelupe? You left without even a word.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: I just thought there wasn't a need to do so.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: Time hasn't been kind to you. The ragazzino told me you're ill?

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: It's not serious, though it's bothersome. My eyes and ears don't work so well anymore, my waist, legs, and shoulder joints are always hurting... it's thanks to my work.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Just elderly things. Even carefully maintained quality fabric will inevitably turn stiff and brittle.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: Take care of your nonno, boy. Don't leave any regrets.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: I didn't expect to meet you here, and what's happened with the boy... has caused you trouble.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: Hardly. I came here for Carnevale, and happened to bump into your grandson here.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: Nonno, I—

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: I know, Luchino. Let me handle this.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: Antonio should have acted in a more decent manner, and I've sent someone to find him so he can explain himself to you.
Antonio... A terribly common name in Siracusa. But right now, Luchino could only match it to a single face—
Antonio Venezia, the head of Venezia Trucking Co.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: ...Signor Antonio?

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: I thought this matter would be more troublesome than this, but since you've already stepped in—

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: Umberto, you lack the patience of your youth.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: Antonio has to explain himself to you, and once that's done, I can also rest easy.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: Do you want to meet the owner of this place, boy?

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: ...Nonno?

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: There's no way we can possibly refuse, is there?

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: Just treat it as a favor to one of your regulars, vecchio amico.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: I was asked before to make a suit for you.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Why don't we make use of our time together here and measure you right now?

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: I hear it's a grand affair, with civilians wearing masks and costumes escorting giant parade cars around the city. I'm sure you'll be there, and need an outfit too.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: I used to remember every regular client's measurements, but as you can see, time shows no mercy to us all. Everyone's changed a lot.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: I've been relying on Luchino more and more to help me write down things I often forget about.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: Alright. We have some time to spare before Antonio arrives.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Luchino, I'm afraid we won't be going back so soon. Can you wait a while longer?

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: It's fine, Nonno! Can I help out somehow?

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Get me my toolbox.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Prepare a file with this gentleman's name on it.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: I'm sorry, signore, I never got your name...
Fabrizio Venezia.
The old man writes down his own name, and gives it to Luchino.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: Y-you're... But why did you say you were a guest...?

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Hush, Luchino. Just do as I say without a word from you, and do what we have to do.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Signor Fabrizio is but a client to us right now.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Would you allow this boy to serve you as my assistant, signore? He's been wanting to work on a major client.
Luchino was never allowed to assist his grandfather with important customers in any step of the process before.
But now, Umberto guides him every step of the way, and even encourages the boy to do it himself.
'You must show your clients respect and gratitude', he is told...
Everything goes smoothly and naturally, as if the kidnapping never happened and his nonno hadn't come here to rescue him.
Just working a regular job.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: His hands are as stable as yours. Will he become a 'tagliatore' like you?

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: A 'tagliatore'?

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: I see you've never told this child about your past, Umberto.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Ingrid, aren't you going in to see Papa?

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: So long as the Don is with them, Umberto and Lucchino won't be in any danger.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: I just have to make sure they walk out of here safe and sound.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: You know that's not what I meant.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: You're the one who he needs to see.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: Involve an innocent child in famiglia affairs? I don't remember the old man ever doing something like this.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: He wasn't brought back here on my orders. But I won't deny it—I would have done this anyway if his presence truly poses a threat to the famiglia's interests.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: The famiglia's interests? Or yours?

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Is there a difference between the two?

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: You've changed quite a lot, Antonio.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: No, you've been away from home for too long, Ingrid.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: This is Siracusa's twenty-third nomadic city. A piece of uncultivated fertile land.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: I've sown seeds here, so I'm obliged to ensure they mature for a ripe harvest. No matter the methods used.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: It's also why I've been urging you to come back to us. I know what you're capable of, and we need you here.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: Anton, the Don won't like this.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: He'll be mad, of course.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: He just summoned me inside, and I can guess he has a lecture in store.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: But do you think he's angry because I got an innocent boy involved? No, he doesn't care at all.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: He's just angry I wasn't stealthy enough, wasn't proper and 'decent' enough.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: I will prove to him with actual results that the Venezias can establish two sets of order at the same time—one on the table and the other underneath.

spans.text: I will prove to him with actual results that the Venezias
establish two sets of order at the same time—one on the table and the other underneath.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: But what we should prioritize is definitely not this so-called 'decency'.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: Even if it hurts him, and those who trust you?

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: I love him, I do. He gave me everything I have. I think this is the way I can repay him for that, no matter what it takes.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: And you got one thing wrong, Ingrid. I've never changed.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: ...Never changed—

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: Is that so...?

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: A 'tagliatore'...

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: De Montano Tailor Shop no longer offers that service today. This child doesn't need to know about it.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: Pity. I still remember how elegantly you would solve my many problems.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: Montelupe's famiglie were all terrified of the elusive 'tagliatore'. One only had to write the target's name down on the order sheet, and he would be reported dead in the newspapers the next day.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: ...It was all to repay your kindness.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: You saved me when I was a young tailor about Luchino's age, and gave me a chance to live in Montelupe.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: You deserve a decent finale, no matter what.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: You've always been so good to me.
Luchino is having a severe headache.
They are indeed, talking about his very own grandfather, but it doesn't seem to match up with the old man right before him.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: Right, what happened to his parents? Your son—Luca, right?

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Yes. Luca de Montano.
Parents? Luchino seems to have asked Umberto about them before, but the old man always dodged the question.
He had tried to read his grandfather's eyes, but the old man only focused on his work.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Luca was a good boy. A wonderful, sensible child with a talent for tailoring and willingness to bear any hardship.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: He was already a pro in his twenties, and the regulars were all fond of him. I had planned to hand over the shop to him.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Until one day, his body was discovered in a vehicle leaving the city early in the morning.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Next to him was a musical actress, with a little bit of fame in Montelupe, highly coveted by many mafiosi—

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Luchino, your hands are shaking.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: ...Perhaps we should slow down?

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Go fetch our fabric samples. I'll handle it from here.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: ...A-Alright.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: ...*sigh*

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: You were a little bit cruel to the boy.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: My days are numbered, signore. I can't protect him forever.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Luca's death made me realize something.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: The blood on my hands can never be wiped clean no matter how many times or ways I try. The stench of it will only bring misfortune to me and my family.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: But that boy still fantasized about serving the so-called 'somebodys'. It's my fault.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Be it Signor Antonio, you, or even other famiglie wise guys, Luchino will eventually run into mafiosi.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: He has to know about it.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: You see Luca's death as punishment for your crimes?

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: As a price I paid...

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Raise your head, signore. To measure your neck circumference.
Nonno would sometimes stay at the workbench longer than usual, and his hands would tremble nonstop.
He teased Luchino on multiple occasions the shop would have to close down if Luchino couldn't learn the trade in time.
But now, his grandfather's hands are steadier than he has ever seen.
Luchino watches him pull out the measuring tape. He starts from Venezia Sr.'s shoulders, and then his arms, chest, waist, and legs.
But Luchino knows his nonno's attention has been on him the whole time.
Unfortunately, he is not yet ready to accept the truth.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: After losing Luca, I learned about Luchino's existence—Luca had him fostered at a farm out in the countryside.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: And then I found out how Luca had met the actress through a costume order from the theater...

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: ...How he hid a forbidden way of life he gradually built for themselves away from everyone, just to save me from worrying and avoid inciting more trouble…

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: ...How he managed to leave a little speck of hope for themselves, and for me...

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Luchino is all I have left from Luca, and my final wish is for him to live.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: No matter what Signor Antonio or you have planned, I beg you—please don't involve him ever again.

steps.name: Luchino
steps.text: (Nonno...)
Luchino does not know how to react.
The truth of his parents' demise, his nonno's past, his own future... he drowns within his web of emotions.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Please raise your arm.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: Sure.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Signore, I do not ask anything of you.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: I only have a selfish wish to give this child some time, to let him carefully observe how a tailor works.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: How to measure, how to cut cloth, how to respectfully receive clients...

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: And how to stay away from a life he doesn't belong in.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: *sigh* Very well. I see you're set on parting from all your history.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: No need to deliver the suit yourself once you're done. I'll get someone to take it from your sartoria.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: Umberto, if you ever feel nostalgic and want to return to Montelupe, make sure to remember il vecchio here too.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Umberto
steps.text: Grazie mille, Signore.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: So, you have no intentions of letting that ragazzino go...

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: Even if the Don's already agreed to do so.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Ingrid, even if the kid swears he won't shoot his mouth off, there's no guarantee city hall won't hear about some ridiculous rumors from him.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Many famiglie have their eyes on us. I can't afford the risk.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Papa will understand.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Think about your family too, Ingrid.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: A wolf asked me to fulfill an agreement we made, and I came back to this country for my daughter.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: My anger has long ceased to burn for the famiglia.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: I act only for my own sake now, Anton.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: ...What a shame. Then I'm afraid there's no more room for any discussion.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: You think they can hold me off?

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: No, I just need to make sure that kid keeps his mouth shut.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: Anton, answer this question.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: When you bailed me out and said you knew who was the culprit behind Lisa's injury, were you telling the truth?

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: ...Absolutely. I've never lied to you, Ingrid.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: After I sent Lisa away from Siracusa, I investigated the matter myself in secret, and although I found nothing...

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: I always had some suspicions I didn't want to admit was possible. Though, I don't think you'll speak any more on the subject, for now at least.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: ...Forgive me, but I can't tell you anything right now.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: No need. I'll find out eventually.
The blade falls just above Antonio's nose, but he retains his smile.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Ingrid, you know there are people watching every move we make in this household.

steps.name: Antonio
steps.text: Such indecent behavior from you.
Ingrid, please lower your blade, for my sake.

steps.name: Ingrid
steps.text: ...Don Venezia.

steps.name: Venezia Sr.
steps.text: Long time no see, child.
